memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Make four gold rings for the table and fasten them to the four corners, where the four legs are. The rings are to be close to the rim to hold the poles used in carrying the table. Make the poles of acacia wood, overlay them with gold and carry the table with them." - Exodus 25:26-28 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Like the ark, the table was fitted with rings and poles so it could be carried. Everything in the tabernacle was built for travel. God's dwelling place among His people was not a fixed temple of stone but a portable tent, designed to move as they moved. Wherever Israel journeyed, the table of God's provision journeyed with them.

This is a quiet comfort. The bread on that table represented God's ongoing provision for His people, and it went with them into every stage of the wilderness. Whatever unfamiliar ground they crossed, the table came too. God's provision was not tied to one location or one season; it travelled with them.

The same is true for you. God's care does not stay behind when your life changes. Whether you move house, change jobs, enter a new season, or face unfamiliar territory, the God who provides goes with you. His faithfulness is not attached to your circumstances but to His own character. Jesus promised to be with us always, to the very end of the age (Matt 28:20). Wherever He leads you next, His provision travels with you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I trust that God's provision goes with me into new and uncertain seasons?
What unfamiliar ground am I facing where I need to remember He travels with me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, Your provision is not tied to my circumstances but to Your faithful character. Thank You that wherever You lead, You go with me and provide for me. Amen.
